title: Green pension envelope arrived? Huwag itabi lang—this monthly top-up needs a claim
summary: FACT: Japan Pension Service began mailing green 年金生活者支援給付金 claim envelopes from September 1, 2026 to basic-pension recipients newly assessed as potentially eligible for the pensioner support benefit. This is not an automatic annual adjustment for newly eligible people: the claim must be submitted. The general rule is that payment starts from the month after a valid claim, so delaying can mean losing payable months outside any applicable special claim window.
why_it_matters: For low-income pension households, this is recurring money rather than a one-time rebate. The FY2026 old-age benefit uses ¥5,620 per month as a base amount, adjusted for contribution/exemption history; Disability Basic Pension recipients can receive ¥5,620 monthly for Grade 2 or ¥7,025 for Grade 1, and the survivor support benefit is ¥5,620 monthly. A green envelope can therefore represent tens of thousands of yen per year, but newly eligible recipients must actually claim it.

claims.text: Japan Pension Service began sending green claim envelopes from September 1, 2026 to basic-pension recipients who are newly able to receive the pensioner support benefit.
claims.basis: JPS September 2026 mailing notice and Pension Committee Topics

claims.text: People who receive the postcard-style claim can submit electronically or by mail; the postcard itself shows the estimated monthly benefit amount if the claim is approved.
claims.basis: JPS claim procedure and estimated-amount instructions

claims.text: The general payment rule is that pensioner support benefit eligibility starts from the month after the claim is submitted, so JPS/MHLW tells eligible people to claim promptly. A special three-month retroactivity rule applies when someone newly acquires a Basic Pension entitlement, but that is not the general rule for every late claim.
claims.basis: MHLW official FAQ on when payment begins after a claim

claims.text: For FY2026, the old-age support benefit uses ¥5,620 per month as its base amount and then adjusts for contribution and exemption periods. Disability support benefit is ¥7,025 per month for Grade 1 and ¥5,620 for Grade 2; survivor support benefit is ¥5,620 per month, subject to its rules.

For the old-age version, the recipient must be 65 or older, receive Old-age Basic Pension, have every member of the same household exempt from municipal resident tax, and meet the applicable prior-year pension/other-income ceiling. Disability and survivor versions use different income tests.

People already receiving the benefit and continuing to meet the requirements generally do not need to submit a new claim every year. The September green-envelope action primarily matters to newly eligible or newly claimable recipients.
Because the envelope resembles routine pension mail and the benefit name is unfamiliar, a household may discard or postpone a claim that can be worth several tens of thousands of yen over a year.
claims.basis: Recurring benefit amount combined with claim-required mailing process

content.policy_status: EFFECTIVE / ACTIVE CLAIM PROCESS. This is an existing statutory benefit, not a newly enacted September policy. The consequential current development is the September 1, 2026 start of claim mailings to people newly assessed as eligible for the 2026 benefit period.
content.key_message: Kung may green envelope mula sa 日本年金機構 na may 年金生活者支援給付金請求書, huwag i-assume na ordinary pension notice lang. For newly eligible people, kailangan mong mag-claim. Delay can matter because the normal rule is payment from the month after your claim.
content.who_is_affected: Basic Pension recipients who are newly eligible for 年金生活者支援給付金. For the old-age version, this generally means age 65+, receiving Old-age Basic Pension, everyone in the same household being exempt from municipal resident tax, and income within the official ceiling. Separate versions exist for qualifying Disability Basic Pension and Survivor Basic Pension recipients.
content.when: Japan Pension Service began sending the 2026 postcard-style claim forms in green envelopes from September 1, 2026. The FY2026 annual eligibility determination is reflected for the October 2026 to September 2027 benefit period. Follow the deadline printed on your own claim form/envelope.
content.financial_impact: Potential recurring household income. FY2026 old-age support uses ¥5,620/month as the base amount before adjusting for contribution/exemption history. That base is ¥67,440 over 12 months if the full base amount applies. Disability Grade 2 and survivor support are ¥5,620/month; Disability Grade 1 is ¥7,025/month. Actual old-age payment can be lower or structured differently depending on pension record and income band.
content.risk_if_ignored: HIGH for someone who received the claim and is eligible: this is recurring benefit money, and the general rule for late claims is payment from the month after the claim. Missing the applicable claim window can therefore permanently lose earlier months rather than simply delay the bank transfer.
content.action: ACT NOW IF THE GREEN ENVELOPE ARRIVES
content.deadline: Use the deadline printed on the 2026 claim form. As of September 6, JPS's public 2026 web page confirms the mailing and claim requirement but does not yet publish one universal grace-date cutoff for every postcard recipient. Do not wait for a national date if your own form already gives one.
content.effort: LOW. The postcard can be mailed after completing the required fields, or eligible recipients of postcard claims can use the electronic procedure described by JPS.
content.potential_benefit: A recurring monthly top-up to the pension while the person continues to meet the requirements, not merely a one-time grant.
content.downside: No legitimate fee is required to claim. Eligibility is limited; receiving a pension alone does not make someone eligible, and old-age benefit amounts vary with pension record and income. A claim can also be denied after review.
content.common_mistake: Thinking JPS will automatically add the money because it already knows your pension and income. Existing recipients who remain eligible generally continue automatically, but a person who receives the new claim form needs to submit it. Another mistake is assuming the ¥5,620 figure is guaranteed for every old-age recipient; it is a base amount used in the calculation.
content.what_to_do_now: If you or an older family member receives a green envelope from Japan Pension Service, open it and look for 年金生活者支援給付金請求書. Check the monthly estimated amount printed on the form. Submit using the enclosed postal procedure or the official electronic route. Keep a photo/copy and the submission date. If the envelope was lost, JPS says the A4 claim form can be downloaded and submitted to a pension office.
content.what_to_wait_for: Do not file a random form just because household income seems low if no eligibility notice has arrived; first confirm the correct benefit category and eligibility with JPS. Also wait for JPS to publish any 2026-specific national late-claim grace cutoff before relying on a date that appeared in a previous year's campaign.
content.strongest_counterinterpretation: This is not a brand-new welfare program and most people already receiving the benefit do not need to act every September. The green-envelope story is consequential only for newly eligible/newly claimable recipients. Some recipients will receive substantially less than ¥5,620/month because the old-age formula depends on contribution history and, for the supplemental tier, income.
content.what_remains_uncertain: JPS's current September 2026 public claim page does not state a single universal late-claim grace cutoff for this year's postcard mailing. The individualized form may contain a deadline, and JPS may publish a 2026-specific FAQ update later. ALAM therefore does not extrapolate last year's January cutoff into 2027 without a current primary document.
content.what_would_change_mind: ALAM would revise this story if JPS announces that 2026 newly eligible recipients are automatically enrolled without a claim, publishes a new retroactivity rule that prevents loss from late filing, materially changes the FY2026 eligibility/payment amounts, or issues a universal 2026 claim cutoff that supersedes the individualized instructions.

reading_levels.30 sec: FACT: From Sept. 1, 2026, Japan Pension Service started sending green claim envelopes to people newly eligible for 年金生活者支援給付金. If yours arrives, submit it—this is not automatically added for newly eligible recipients. FY2026's old-age benefit uses ¥5,620/month as a base amount, while actual payment depends on pension record/income. Normal rule: benefit starts from the month after claim, so delaying can lose payable months.
reading_levels.2 min: Japan Pension Service's September mailing targets Basic Pension recipients newly assessed as able to receive the pensioner support benefit. The important fine print is procedural: existing recipients who stay eligible generally continue without a yearly claim, but newly eligible people receive a green envelope and must submit the claim. The postcard shows an estimated monthly amount and can be submitted by mail or, for qualifying postcard recipients, electronically. For FY2026 the old-age scheme uses ¥5,620/month as a base amount, while disability Grade 2 and survivor support are ¥5,620/month and disability Grade 1 is ¥7,025/month. MHLW says the general rule is payment from the month after the claim, which means procrastination can cost earlier months. Follow the deadline printed on your own 2026 form; do not rely on last year's cutoff unless JPS republishes it for this year's mailing.

outcomes: Recognize the green JPS envelope as a benefit claim rather than routine pension correspondence.
Understand that newly eligible recipients need to claim while continuing recipients usually do not reapply annually.
Know why filing timing matters and why ¥5,620 is not a guaranteed old-age payment for everyone.
learning.background: 年金生活者支援給付金 is a permanent income-support top-up paid alongside pension benefits to qualifying lower-income pension recipients. JPS rechecks eligibility using income/household information. When someone becomes newly eligible, JPS can send a claim form rather than simply starting the benefit automatically.

terms.term: 年金生活者支援給付金
terms.meaning: A recurring support payment added to qualifying basic-pension recipients' income.
terms.why_it_matters: It can provide several thousand yen per month but newly eligible recipients generally need to claim it.

terms.term: 補足的老齢年金生活者支援給付金
terms.meaning: A supplemental old-age support tier for people whose pension/other income is above the main old-age threshold but still within the official upper band.
terms.why_it_matters: It prevents a sharp cliff at the main income threshold, so some people slightly above it can still receive a smaller payment.

takeaways: Green JPS envelope from September 2026: open it and check whether it is a support-benefit claim.
Newly eligible recipients must act; existing recipients generally do not reapply every year if still eligible.
Filing late can shift the payment start date under the normal rule.
The old-age ¥5,620 figure is a calculation base, not a universal guaranteed payment.

action_plan.goal: Avoid losing months of a legitimate recurring pension support benefit because a claim envelope was ignored.
action_plan.who_should_act: Anyone receiving the green 年金生活者支援給付金 claim envelope from Japan Pension Service, or a family member helping an older/disabled pension recipient manage official mail.
action_plan.deadline: Submit by the deadline printed on the claim form. Earlier is safer because the general benefit-start rule depends on the claim month.

steps.action: Look for the green Japan Pension Service envelope and the words 年金生活者支援給付金請求書.
steps.how: Check official JPS branding and compare with the example shown on the JPS website.
steps.done_when: You know whether the mailing is the support-benefit claim.

steps.step: Check the estimated amount and deadline
steps.action: Read the estimated monthly payment printed on the postcard and the submission deadline shown in your packet.
steps.how: Do not substitute a deadline found in an old article for the date on the current form.
steps.done_when: You know the expected monthly value and your actual deadline.

steps.action: Use JPS's official electronic procedure if available to you, or complete and mail the postcard as instructed.
steps.how: Keep a photo/copy and note the submission date. If lost, use JPS's downloadable A4 claim form or contact the pension office.
steps.done_when: The claim has been electronically submitted or posted and you retained proof/date.
